step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates a serverless and event-driven data ingestion, storage, querying, and prediction platform (DUKC platform by OMC International). Data flows through three main logical pathways: 1) Data Ingestion and Archival Stream: Port Sensors transmit environmental readings into Amazon MSK. An AWS Lambda function reads messages from MSK via event source mapping and writes hot data into a DynamoDB table (with a 3-month TTL). DynamoDB Streams capture changes and send them to Kinesis Data Firehose, which archives data in Parquet format to an S3 Bucket (Historical). 2) User Query Path: External Users or consuming platforms make requests via Amazon API Gateway, which triggers a Query Lambda function. Depending on the age and volume of data, Lambda queries either DynamoDB (for hot data) or Amazon Athena (for historical data in S3). 3) Prediction Layer: An ECS containerized prediction service generates forecasts and outputs prediction files to an S3 Bucket (Predictions).

graph.name: OMC International DUKC Platform Serverless Architecture
graph.notes: Achieved 30x increase in processing speed/scale and 10-15% cost savings using serverless architecture with DynamoDB TTL (3 months) and S3 Parquet historical archiving.

nodes.name: Port Sensors
nodes.notes: External sensors collecting environmental data such as wind, wave, and tide.

nodes.name: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
nodes.notes: Ingests environmental sensor messages streaming from port sensors.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda function (Ingestion)
nodes.notes: Processes sensor data from MSK via event source mapping.

nodes.name: DynamoDB Table
nodes.notes: Hot storage location with a 3-month Time-To-Live (TTL).

nodes.name: DynamoDB Stream
nodes.notes: Captures change events from the DynamoDB table.

nodes.name: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose
nodes.notes: Converts change events to Parquet format and delivers to historical S3 storage.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 Bucket (Historical)
nodes.notes: Stores historical sensor data long term in Parquet format.

nodes.name: Users
nodes.notes: External users and platforms requesting data.

nodes.name: Amazon API Gateway
nodes.notes: Entry point for query requests from users and platforms.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda function (Query)
nodes.notes: Routes query requests dynamically based on requested data age and volume.

nodes.name: Amazon Athena
nodes.notes: Executes SQL queries against historical data stored in the S3 bucket.

nodes.name: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)
nodes.notes: Containerized prediction service forecasting up to two weeks of data.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 Bucket (Predictions)
nodes.notes: Stores predictions generated by the ECS prediction service.

edges.notes: Port sensors stream environmental readings into Amazon MSK.
MSK triggers ingestion Lambda function via event source mapping.
Ingestion Lambda function writes processed messages into DynamoDB hot storage.
DynamoDB streams table changes to DynamoDB Stream.
DynamoDB Stream forwards change log events to Kinesis Data Firehose.
Firehose transforms and writes historical data into S3 in Parquet format.
Users send requests to API Gateway.
API Gateway invokes query Lambda function.
Query Lambda fetches recent/hot data from DynamoDB.
Query Lambda invokes Athena for historical data queries.
Amazon Athena queries historical files in S3 bucket.
ECS prediction service writes forecasted data to S3 bucket.
